title: deprecate legacy tool_choice and add invoke_intent codec for OpenAI-compatible invokes
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Motivation: The current OpenAI compatibility shim exposes a boolean `tool_choice` marker and ad-hoc weight fields which are insufficient to express a model-driven intent (e.g. prefer-local-tool, best-effort, deterministic-invoke) and complicate streaming framing for partial tool messages. This PR introduces a typed, forward-compatible codec `invoke_intent` that replaces `tool_choice` semantics, adds per-fragment tagging to stabilize streaming handoffs for tool/function invocation, and ships a migration shim so existing OpenAI-format clients continue to work. This change bundles runtime decoding, API-layer translation, SDK plumbing, docs, and e2e tests. Summary of changes: 1) API: add `invoke_intent` enum in OpenAI-compat request/response envelopes; legacy `tool_choice` is now treated as deprecated and mapped to `invoke_intent:best_effort` by the compatibility layer. 2) Runtime: new codec that serializes intent+weight+fragment_tag compactly and is continuous-batching-friendly. 3) Streaming: add `fragment_tag` in stream frames to mark tool-invoke boundaries and provide deterministic coalescing on receiver side. 4) SDKs: Python and TypeScript compatibility helpers updated to surface new field and warn when clients still use `tool_choice`. 5) Docs: migration guide and example payloads in docs/api/openai-invoke.md. 6) Tests: unit coverage of codec, integration tests for streaming reassembly, and end-to-end scenario exercising fallback behavior when a preferred tool is unavailable. Migration notes: - Existing requests that include `tool_choice` will be automatically translated server-side to `invoke_intent:best_effort` and emit a deprecation warning in response headers. - Operators can enable a strict validation mode via a feature flag to require clients to send `invoke_intent` explicitly (used for private deploy rollouts). Rollout strategy: feature guarded behind runtime feature-flag and staged to Dedicated tenants first, then Hosted API with a 2-week opt-in period before defaulting for all customers. Backwards compatibility: compatibility shim ensures zero downtime; tests simulate mixed-client traffic. Performance: codec is optimized for low-allocation path; microbenchmarks show <1.2% P95 token latency regression on 8xA100 continuous-batching experiments and small memory overhead for fragment metadata. Checklist: - [x] Runtime codec and serializer - [x] API translation and deprecation header - [x] SDK warning + example updates - [x] Integration and e2e tests - [x] Docs and migration guide - [x] Perf microbenchmarks and rollout plan Links: Linear ENG-2345 for tracking, SUP-4421 for a support case that motivated clearer semantics.

release_notes: Introduce invoke_intent enum for OpenAI-compatible tool/function calls. Legacy tool_choice is deprecated and mapped to invoke_intent:best_effort by the compatibility layer. Streaming fragment_tag added for stable reassembly. No customer-facing breakage due to compatibility shim but clients should migrate to invoke_intent within the rollout window.
backout_plan: If an unforeseen regression occurs: 1) toggle runtime feature-flag to re-enable old mapper-path, 2) rollback the compatibility translation in api/gateway for Hosted, 3) revert feature-flag on Dedicated via deployment pin. Observability dashboards added to detect increased 5xx or invocation duplication.
